w10_T4_001717: Nora's lunch bowl recipe uses 95 grams of rice, 80 grams of lentils, and 39 grams of roasted vegetables in every bowl. Her friend Finn, who eats less, makes his bowls with exactly half the amount of food that one of Nora's bowls contains, so Nora's bowl is the heavier of the two. The recipe comes from a cookbook with 60 pages. Finn prepares 8 bowls a day for his food stall, and he runs the stall 7 days a week. He weighs everything in grams even though he buys his ingredients by the kilogram, and he knows that one thousand grams make a kilogram. How many grams of food does Finn prepare for his stall in one week?
w10_T4_001719: A conference keynote was planned to last 48 minutes, but the organiser cut 12 minutes for the opening speech and 24 minutes for the sponsor video. The remaining time was shared equally among 6 presenters, so each presenter got the same short slot. On top of that slot, every presenter is given 57 minutes of questions from the audience. Ana is one of the presenters, and she repeats her full slot plus questions once a day on each of the 7 days of the conference. The schedule is written in minutes rather than hours, since sixty minutes make one hour. How many minutes does Ana spend on stage over the whole conference?
w10_T4_001724: In the morning Grace picked 76 strawberries at the farm and then 57 more before the sun got hot. Her brother Hugo, working the bigger field, picked 6 times as many strawberries as Grace did all morning, so his basket was far heavier than hers. In the afternoon Hugo sold 128 of his strawberries to a passing cyclist. In the evening he sold every strawberry he had left at the village market for 3 cents each. How many cents did Hugo earn at the market?
w10_T4_001726: A vending machine at the station sells a bag of pretzels for 92 cents. In January the price went up by 27 cents, and in February the operator ran a promotion that cut 80 cents off the price. In March a 25-cent levy was added to every bag. Lily then bought 4 bags at the March price and paid entirely in cents rather than dollars, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents did Lily pay?
w10_T4_001728: In the morning a market stall had 17 melons on display. The stallholder sold 11 melons before ten o'clock and 4 more just before lunch. In the afternoon a farmer delivered 46 melons to the stall. In the evening the stallholder cut every melon she had into 4 equal wedges to sell at the night market. How many wedges did she have for the night market?
w10_T4_001736: On Monday morning a bottling line was set up with 4 identical lanes, each filling 112 bottles every minute. At midday the foreman added a hand-fed station that filled 15 more bottles every minute alongside the lanes. In the afternoon the line ran in cycles of 8 minutes, with 7 cycles in every hour of work, and the working day lasted 7 hours in all. In the evening, after the line had stopped, an inspector filled 8 extra bottles by hand as samples. How many bottles were filled in total that day?
w10_T4_001737: Mia had 154 dollars in her savings account and then deposited another 16 dollars. Her cousin Noah had twice as much money as Mia had after that deposit, so Noah was the richer of the two. Noah's grandmother, who thinks in dollars rather than cents because one hundred cents to the dollar is too fiddly for her, then doubled whatever Noah had. The electronics shop is 15 minutes from Noah's house. Noah spent 547 dollars there on a laptop. How many dollars does Noah have left?
w10_T4_001739: Kai's video clip was 127 seconds long. He added a 3-second title card at the start, then cut out a 99-second scene that dragged, and trimmed another 3 seconds of dead air. Finally he added 35 seconds of credits at the end. Kai edits in seconds rather than minutes, even though the sharing site displays the length in minutes, since sixty seconds make one minute. How many seconds long is the finished clip?
w10_T4_001742: In the morning, the print room at Elm Street School ran off 80 worksheets for each class, and there are 3 classes in every year group and 7 year groups in the school. In the afternoon the head teacher asked for exactly the same print run to be repeated on each of the 8 days of the exam fortnight. In the evening the district office decided that all 5 schools in the district would follow the same plan. How many worksheets will be printed across the district over the exam period?
w10_T4_001747: Eli earned 78 dollars in his first week at the cafe but spent 32 dollars of it on a uniform. Rosa, the head waitress, took home triple what Eli had left, and that was her pay for 6 days of work at the same wage each day. On top of her daily wage Rosa makes 37 dollars a day in tips. She then worked 9 more days at that daily wage plus tips, and spent 100 dollars of it on a coat. How many dollars did Rosa keep from those 9 days?
w10_T4_001752: On Saturday morning Kim baked 154 cupcakes for the charity fair, and Jun, who runs a much bigger stall, baked 9 times as many cupcakes as Kim did. Jun's stall is 12 metres long. In the afternoon Jun gave 244 cupcakes to the local shelter and sold 1137 cupcakes to visitors. In the evening a customer brought back 4 cupcakes that had been bought by mistake. How many cupcakes did Jun have left at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_001760: The Harbour Hotel has 8 floors with 31 rooms on each floor. On the festival weekend 235 of the rooms were already booked, and every room that was still free had 4 beds in it. The hotel has 3 lifts. To cope with the crowds, the manager brought in 71 camp beds and 39 sofa beds, all of them free to book. Then a tour group arrived and took 125 of the free beds. How many free beds were left?
w10_T4_001761: In the morning a plant nursery counted 199 tomato seedlings in its first tray and then added 52 more seedlings to it. There were 2 trays like that on each shelf, both filled the same way, and 6 shelves in the first greenhouse. In the afternoon the staff confirmed that all 3 of their greenhouses were stocked identically. Each greenhouse is 40 metres long. In the evening all of the seedlings were shared equally among 3 garden centres. How many seedlings did the Oakfield garden centre receive?
w10_T4_001764: Tara has collected 232 bottle caps, which she keeps in a dozen glass jars. Her sister Uma has 9 times as many bottle caps as Tara, so Uma's collection is much larger. Over the summer Uma found 40 caps at the beach, 32 caps at a festival, and 36 caps behind the corner shop. She then handed 1954 caps over to a recycling drive. How many bottle caps does Uma have now?
w10_T4_001773: On Saturday morning Vic had 128 dollars in his wallet and spent 67 dollars at the grocery store. His flatmate Wen had 3 times as much money as Vic had left after shopping, so Wen was clearly better off. In the afternoon Wen paid 164 dollars to have his bike repaired. In the evening Wen received 80 dollars from a client and 63 dollars from selling an old lamp. How many dollars does Wen have now?
w10_T4_001775: At eight o'clock there were 52 cars in the stadium car park. Over the next hour 72 cars arrived, and then 98 cars left when the morning event finished. Later 15 cars arrived for the afternoon session, 11 cars left before the break, and another 16 cars left after it. The car park has 2 entrances. How many cars are in the car park now?
w10_T4_001779: In the morning at Sana's coffee cart, 8 regulars each left a tip of 112 cents in the jar. A tourist then dropped in 79 cents and a delivery driver added 50 cents. In the afternoon Sana took 30 cents out of the jar for a parking meter and paid 456 cents from it for a sandwich. In the evening a customer put in 3 cents of change. Sana counts her tips in cents rather than dollars, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents are in the tip jar at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_001783: Xavier and Yara entered an arcade tournament, one of a dozen held in the city that year. Their team's 141 tokens were shared equally among 3 players, and Xavier was one of them. Xavier used 37 of his tokens on the racing game and then lost 3 tokens down a drain, so at that point he held fewer tokens than Yara, who had been more careful with hers. In the bonus round every token Xavier still held was worth 9 points, and a penalty for a late finish then took 20 points away. How many points did Xavier end with?
w10_T4_001787: In the morning a wholesale market received a shipment of rice: each pallet held a 69-kilogram sack and a 50-kilogram sack, there were 4 pallets in each truck, and 8 trucks arrived. The warehouse is 20 kilometres from the port. In the afternoon 3587 kilograms of the rice were sold to restaurants. In the evening the manager sold all of the remaining rice to a single buyer at 4 dollars per kilogram, plus a delivery charge of 77 dollars. He weighs rice in kilograms rather than grams, since one thousand grams make a kilogram. How many dollars did the buyer pay in total?
w10_T4_001798: Zack had 108 minutes of talk time left on his phone plan. He used 85 minutes on a call to his grandmother and another 6 minutes calling a taxi. His sister Ava, one of a dozen cousins in the family group chat, had 5 times as many minutes left as Zack did after those calls, so Ava was much better off. Ava then used 74 minutes on a work call and 3 minutes confirming a dentist appointment. The plan shows the balance in minutes rather than hours, and sixty minutes make one hour. How many minutes of talk time does Ava have left?
w10_T4_001799: In the morning Cleo picked 173 cherries from the tree in her garden and handed 139 of them over the fence to her neighbour. In the afternoon she picked 42 more cherries. Her brother Dev, who had been picking at the orchard all day, came home with triple the number of cherries Cleo had at that point, so Dev had far more than his sister. In the evening Dev sold 119 of his cherries at the roadside stand. How many cherries does Dev have now?
w10_T4_001806: Emma has 14 merit badges on her sash. Her friend Felix has twice as many badges as Emma, so Felix is ahead of her. Over the year Felix earned 66 badges at summer camp, 37 badges for community service, and another 37 badges for his hiking challenge. He then decided to divide all of his badges equally among the 6 members of his new patrol, one of whom is Gus. How many badges did Gus receive?
w10_T4_001813: In the morning Iris checked the bus fare, which is 153 cents per trip, and found that her student card takes 34 cents off every trip. She makes 7 trips a week. In the afternoon she decided to load her card for twice that long, 2 whole weeks of trips. In the evening she topped up the card, which charges a 57-cent fee for the top-up. She counts in cents rather than dollars, knowing that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents did the top-up cost her altogether?
w10_T4_001819: In the morning Jo had a 156-minute shift ahead of her, of which 121 minutes were booked for meetings. She split the remaining time equally into 5 short breaks. In the afternoon she took 5 breaks of exactly that length. In the evening she worked out that she would keep to the same break pattern on each of the next 9 working days. She measures breaks in minutes rather than hours, since sixty minutes make an hour. How many minutes of breaks will Jo take over those 9 days?
w10_T4_001830: Ken's pear orchard produced 7 crates of pears with 169 pears in each crate, which was more than his neighbour Lars managed from his whole orchard that season. Ken then found 12 pears that had fallen into the grass and picked 69 more from a late tree. He sold 106 pears to a jam maker and afterwards picked 51 more from the last row. He then sold every pear he had at the wholesale market for 5 cents each. How many cents did Ken receive at the wholesale market?
